messages.subject: lavPredict: "Error in if (prob < .Machine$double.eps) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed"
parts:
Dear lavaan community,

I'm struggling to understand this error:

> predictions <- lavPredict(semFit)
Error in if (prob < .Machine$double.eps) { : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

It clearly occurs at line 801 of lav_predict.R, so I went on a little journey to understand why...

After taking that script apart, it appears that the error occurs because the object `prob` is `NaN`. This is because `p1` and `p2` are `NaN`. Those are `NaN` because `YHAT`, estimated by computeEYetax.LISREL in line 771, is `NaN`, and that's `NaN` because the `eta.i` being passed to computeEYetax.LISREL is `NaN`. `eta.i` (I think) gets estimated by the `nlminb` optimization function itself.

So, the source of the error traces back to `nlminb` optimization. This leads me to believe that the optimization is failing to find the maximum likelihood. I've tried `BFGS` instead of `nlminb`, but same error. My best guess is that there's some unusual or weak covariance in my data, but I'm having a hard time identifying it. I can't produce a MRE, so I have attached the entire lavaan object.

What can I do to understand why `nlminb` is failing? Is there a work-around that I can employ?

Thanks,
David
